title: WHEN A LAMB IS BEYOND REACH

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Anyone who cannot afford a lamb is to bring two doves or two young pigeons to the LORD as a penalty for their sin—one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering. They are to bring them to the priest, who shall first offer the one for the sin offering.'" - Lev 5:7-8a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again, God comes down a step. Cannot afford a lamb? Bring two birds.

This has now happened in every chapter we have read. God will not allow poverty to become a barrier between a person and forgiveness. He keeps writing another clause, opening another door, naming another option.

Sit with the implication. In Israel's system, the price of forgiveness was adjusted so that everyone could pay it. Which means forgiveness was never really about the price at all. God set the terms so that the terms could always be met.

That is a picture of grace built into law. And it prepares us for the moment when God removed the cost entirely by bearing it Himself. Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters; and you who have no money, come, buy and eat! (Isa 55:1). Without money and without cost.

Notice too the order: the sin offering first, then the burnt offering. Sin dealt with, then consecration. Cleansing before commitment. God does not ask you to give Him your whole life before He deals with your guilt. He forgives, and then He receives you.

If you have been waiting until you are better to come to God — that is not the order He gave.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I believed that something about my circumstances puts God's forgiveness out of reach?
2. Am I trying to consecrate my life before letting God cleanse it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You set the price where I could reach it, and then paid it Yourself in Christ. I come to You as I am today. Amen.
